findings.text: the lifetime deadline is re-anchored at every reload, so the guard stops guarding exactly when it is needed. _FollowerReloader.poll replaces this process with os.execv(sys.executable, [sys.executable, "-c", launcher, *sys.argv[1:]]) at reckon/cli.py:1731-1737, which passes the original arguments through, so the replacement image re-parses --lifetime 29m and started_at = clock() here restarts the whole grant. Against the host's thirty-minute cap a reloaded 29m follower reaches the cap first and no follower-end line is ever delivered, which is the failure this section exists to prevent and the case it was written for, since a reload fires precisely while code is landing. The plan's own section 8, added on 2026-09-23 after this section was used in a live session, records that expiry as measured and owns the repair by carrying an absolute deadline across the image replacement; at this revision the code path is exactly as that section describes it, and nothing in the gate exercises a reload.

the attach-line assertion cannot fail on the clause the done-when names, because it compares the follower's final line against a fresh call to runs._watch_attach_line, the same production function the line was composed from. It can therefore detect a mangled splice and nothing else: at this revision the line carries the bare word reckon rather than an absolute path, and the gate is green anyway. I proved the bare word by mutating _needs_you_runs to name nobody, whose failure output quotes the line verbatim as "follower end: arming lifetime elapsed; re-arm with: reckon crew follow --project proj --session s1; no runs need you". Making that token absolute is section 2's change, which was in flight while this node ran, so the clause is only satisfiable once section 2 lands; the coordinator should know the gate will stay green through that landing without asserting the clause at all.

item_verdicts.diff: read both commits against base 3794cd2a; b48fdc21 adds the lifetime option, the two line-composing helpers and the deadline reads on the wait pass in reckon/cli.py, and 181e2671 adds the section 3 landing comment, the evidence record and the figure; git diff --numstat 3794cd2a..181e2671 returns exactly the six declared paths and nothing else.
item_verdicts.done_when: I re-ran the named gate myself from the reviewed tree at f0ce63a9, which carries reckon/cli.py and tests/test_follow_lifetime.py byte-identical to 181e2671: 2 passed in 20.26s, EXIT=0, logged at rereview-gate.log. Four of the five clauses hold as written - the test arms with --lifetime 3s over a one-unpromoted-run fixture, observes exit status 0, asserts the last line is marked as the follower's end, names that run's node and the released registration, and the no-lifetime test holds the follower past five seconds. Two clauses do not: the five-second bound is measured from the arm rather than from spawn, disclosed in evidence_inputs with n=5 measurements of 5.53-6.42 s wall for a 3 s grant, and the last line names a bare reckon rather than the absolute attach line, because absoluteness belongs to section 2 and was not landed at this revision.
item_verdicts.goal: the node goal is that a follower armed with --lifetime reaches its own deadline first, prints one line a reader can act on, and releases its registration; at 181e2671 reckon/cli.py:2189 adds --lifetime, :1899-1914 reads the deadline on the wait pass, :2037-2043 yields the follower-end event, :2279-2285 prints it as written rather than as a fleet row, and :1757 marks it follower-end so it does not read as a fleet transition. I confirmed the mechanism end to end by re-running the gate, and separately confirmed the run-listing clause is not vacuous by mutating _needs_you_runs to name nobody and watching the gate redden on that assertion alone. The clause about the host's notice arriving after a line the reader can act on fails in one case I verified by reading the code path: a reload restarts the deadline, so the host's cap can land first.
item_verdicts.manifest: read at the run directory against its live pointer; status complete with commits b48fdc21 and 181e2671 and base 3794cd2a, a declared negative_control_log whose first line is the mutation string, evidence_inputs carrying five wall-clock samples per grant and the arm-anchored bound stated as a disclosed deviation, follow_ons naming the adjacent pre-existing failure and the section 2 dependency, and blockers naming the sixty-minute fence breach honestly at roughly 3h15m rather than absorbing it.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the declared set at orientation is reckon/cli.py, tests/test_follow_lifetime.py, the evidence archive page, the figure directory and the plan; git diff --numstat 3794cd2a..181e2671 returns exactly 164/1 on reckon/cli.py, 245/0 on tests/test_follow_lifetime.py, 80/0 on docs/evidence/archive/a-follower-outlives-its-monitor-landed.html, 83/0 and one binary on the figure directory and 3/0 on docs/plans/a-follower-outlives-its-monitor.html, with plan-version and plan-modified untouched.

justifications.durability: the gate is a real one - two tests over real subprocesses under a temporary RECKON_HOME, asserting exit status, the last line's content, the released registration, and that the shared config home is untouched - and both directions of falsification were demonstrated: the node's own control reddens the lifetime mechanism, and my mutation of the needs-you listing reddens the run-naming assertion with the line quoted verbatim, so neither is vacuous. Two deductions follow from what the gate cannot see. The attach-line assertion at tests/test_follow_lifetime.py:206 is self-referential, comparing the composed line against the composing function, so the done-when's absolute clause is unguarded and is in fact unmet at this revision while the gate stays green. And the deadline does not survive the follower's own reload, so the guard silently stops firing in the one circumstance it was written for. A minor third: assert NODE in final at :212 anchors on the two-character literal n1, which a future absolute attach line could match by accident.
justifications.evidence: the gate is the file the done-when names and I re-ran it independently at a tree carrying that file byte-identical to the reviewed head, 2 passed in 20.26s, rather than take the record's word; the declared negative control is executed, logged, and genuinely reddens with its own mechanism message quoted, and the node ran it at base with the mutation and records both. The attribution of the one adjacent failure is sound and I confirmed it rather than accepted it: the id reproduces on its own at f0ce63a9 (1 failed in 4.28s), and both reckon/crew/node.py and tests/test_crew_session_delivery.py are absent from the base-to-head numstat, so the failure is necessarily present at base and the added-failure count of 0 is correct. Deductions: head-gate.log names its revision and command but no tree path, and regression-follow-adjacent.log carries no header at all, opening on a pytest progress row - which the node itself discloses rather than hides.
justifications.fit: the new code keeps the file's idiom rather than importing another: a module-level comment stating why the stream's fleet-only vocabulary gets one exception, docstrings that give the mechanism and the reason (the deadline read on the wait pass exists because a follower with no producer must still reach it), and the private cross-module helper access that this package already uses throughout. Every new name describes what it does - FOLLOWER_END_EVENT, _needs_you_runs, _follower_end_line, _follower_end_event - and none carries a plan, sprint, stage or ticket label. Ruff check on reckon/cli.py reports 4 findings at base and 4 at head, so the commit adds none, and both changed source paths are ruff format clean. The test module's docstring states the arm-anchored bound as a measurement rather than as a preference.
justifications.goal_fidelity: four of the section's clauses land cleanly and were verified by running them: the option exists and takes a duration, the deadline is read on the wait pass so a quiet session still reaches it, the line is marked follower-end rather than read as a fleet transition, and the registration is released rather than left to be discovered dead. The run-listing clause is real and not vacuous, for the highest confidence in the review - my mutation of the listing reddened exactly that assertion. Two clauses fall short. The line names the attach line rather than the absolute attach line, the latter being section 2's change and still in flight, so at this revision the done-when's own word absolute is unmet. And the section's headline promise - that the host's notice arrives after a line the reader can act on - does not hold across a reload, which is the case the section was written for, and which the plan's section 8 recorded as measured in production.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --numstat 3794cd2a..181e2671 is exactly the six paths the orientation declared, the plan carries a 3-line insertion-only comment with plan-version and plan-modified untouched, and no shared index or sprint state is mutated. The one path that could have gone wrong is the evidence archive, which is a cumulative record other nodes also write into: it is absent at base, so this node created it, and I checked the merge rather than the branch - the main checkout's copy at e32d0d4a holds both id=s3 and id=s6 at 146 lines, so neither section displaced the other. The figure directory is likewise shared and the two nodes' files do not collide. The reviewed head is 181e2671, matching the revision pinned in this node's second write path.
